0.content:
Gaming's father, a tea merchant of Qiaoying Village whose family had grown tea for generations before he turned to selling leaves. He wanted Gaming to inherit the business and saw Wushou Dance as a road to poverty and injury. After his wife's death the two drifted apart; when Gaming was hurt yet again, Tak gave away all his son's equipment except the beast head his wife had made, and Gaming left home the next day. Tak secretly asked Communications Office contacts to look out for him and had the assistant Leong write festive letters, but would not swallow his pride. He blamed himself for his wife's illness and dreaded anything happening to their only son; in 4.4 he confided his worries about Gaming's dangerous, unstable life to Zhongli. After watching Gaming's Lantern Rite performance he dropped his opposition and called him a great kid; Gaming hugged him.

By the next winter Tak was dragging Gaming to the market for birthday hotpot ingredients and cooking the Nine Great Dishes. He is an excellent cook. He keeps a Money Tree at home and checks on it every morning, and still bangs on Gaming's door when the boy and Man Chai sound like they are fighting.

1.comment: Gaming: Gaming's mother and her letter
1.content:
His unnamed mother married into Qiaoying Village from afar and helped build the tea business. Gaming followed her everywhere as a child and took her speech, her love of dim sum, herbal teas and greens. She supported his Wushou Dance and made his beast head. She died of illness. Her only letter to him, which he keeps folded in a book under his pillow, asks him not to quarrel with his father ("more bark than bite"), to be careful and dress warmly, to keep his promises, to treat true friends sincerely, and not to bottle up his feelings. She told him he was better than char siu after all. The book was her teacup coaster; he admits she never read it either.

He never cries about her in front of others. Alone, he jokes, the wind always blows sand into his eyes, even indoors. The anecdote dish Golden-Tempered Jade, taught to him by Leong, was one of her favourites.

2.content:
A small red suanni, a young member of the solitary Illuminated Beasts of Chenyu Vale's mountains. Gaming sought a real suanni at Mt. Lingmeng for Wushou inspiration, brought his beast head and a bag of offerings, and was surprised and delighted to find a cute tiny creature on a rock. When he tried to pat it, it attacked him like a living flame, and Gaming instinctively danced against it with his beast head until dusk, copying its moves. It accepted him, and the troupe was founded that day. Man Chai has followed him since.

Man Chai is hyperactive and mischievous: knocks over tea, moshes to Xinyan's music, paces on the desk while Gaming writes letters, and "can't read". Gaming credits watching him for better suanni movements. The suanni Lingyuan knows that a youngling of its kin chose to walk with a human out of curiosity.

3.content: Gaming once shared his provisions with a stranger resting by a lake and told her she seemed a wise elder more worthy of respect than the adepti. She was the adeptus Cloud Retainer (he knew she was an adeptus; she now lives in Liyue Harbor as Xianyun), and she was so pleased she resolved to look out for him. In 4.4 she learned of his rift with his father and planned a reconciliation: she had Charlotte buy Tak's tea for Fontaine, sent father and son on the escort, had Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver stage a bandit attack, and used adeptal wind to make his Lantern Rite performance spectacular. He calls her "Aunty Xianyun"; she remade his worn beast head (after he talked her down from ten new giant ones).

4.comment: Gaming: The Mighty Mythical Beasts and Wushou Dance
4.content:
Wushou Dance is a Chenyu Vale folk art in which dancers in a beast head and blanket portray a suanni, to drums and cymbals, sometimes on high Plum Blossom Poles. In Liyue Harbor it is a newish curiosity, less beloved than Liyue opera. Gaming founded the Mighty Mythical Beasts after meeting Man Chai and is its head; the wiki also lists Dip Yeuk, a Yilong Wharf local, as a member. His goal is to make Wushou Dance a regular sight in Liyue Harbor, then to bring it to all of Teyvat. Equipment wears out quickly and costs a lot.

The troupe's 4.4 Lantern Rite show was a hit, but in 6.3 Gaming admitted recruitment was "seriously struggling" because the art is so physically demanding. His fellow guards all tried it once because it "looked totally dope"; almost none kept it up.

key: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency
5.comment: Gaming: Sword and Strongbox Secure Transport Agency
5.content:
An escort agency based in Yilong Wharf, a sub-organisation of the Communications Office, whose guards protect merchants' cargo and travellers on Liyue's roads. Gaming is its "Gold-Standard Guard", the one who can keep clients happy and beat brigands. Zhigui works there. Longzhou of the Communications Office assigns him jobs from Liyue Harbor.

Gaming joined as a temp around a Lantern Rite after bringing in a Fontainian client, and was hired permanently. His colleagues tease him for treating overtime as relaxation but bought him Plum Blossom Poles for his birthday. He brings Bubu Pharmacy medicine back for them.

6.content: Gaming once mistook a shiny stone from Man Chai's mane for a Vision. His real one came later: escorting a caravan, he refused the merchants' advice to abandon the cargo, held off about ten bandits alone until the Millelith arrived, and collapsed. The merchants found an unlisted Vision in their goods and sent it with a thank-you plaque. Gaming feared it meant he should quit dancing, until the plaque's alert, auspicious beast made him see that protecting people was the suanni's spirit. He jokes that receiving it felt like a kung-fu novel's opening of the energy meridians, then admits he is just "a good neighbor" with extra energy.

key: Vibrant Harriers Aloft in Spring Breeze
The Glede Returns to the Pavilion
7.content: Limited-time Lantern Rite event, February 2024. Gaming took the Traveler and Paimon on a delivery to Yilong Wharf, where they sneaked past a crowd of his relatives shopping in the street. Over dim sum at Xinyue Kiosk he explained his dream and the near fistfight with his father. At Xianyun's kite workshop he took Shuyu and Yaoyao home and was overheard muttering that a kite can never be free of the ground. Xianyun's plan followed: Gaming escorted his own father, chased off "bandits" Houzhang and Jiehu (Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper in disguise), and guessed they were fake. Zhongli, not in on it, told Tak that holding a kite too tight stops it from rising. At the festival the harbour lanterns dimmed for his entrance and he leapt up a ladder of Xiao Lanterns in a spectacular Wushou show; his father told him he had always been a great kid, and Gaming hugged him.

8.content: Limited-time Lantern Rite event, early 2026. Making a Xiao Lantern, Gaming wished for apprentices; Lu Xiangxiang popped up begging to join, and he joked the White Horse Adeptus worked fast. She was being taken over by Zizhi, a Deadly Self of the adeptus Zibai, which then jumped into Gaming. Possessed, he snapped at Paimon, chased two Treasure Hoarders out of the city threatening them into becoming his apprentices, and tried to recruit the disguised Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver. Moon Carver expelled the spirit (into Mountain Shaper). Told what he had done, Gaming was so mortified he asked for his dad to throw a slipper at him and fainted from exhaustion; Moon Carver carried him back. He recovered in time to watch the lunar eclipse and release lanterns.

9.content: Gaming and the rattan-weaver Lan Yan have known each other since childhood in Chenyu Vale. She remembers him as the neighbourhood terror who has since matured and still carries snacks everywhere; he remembers her helping him repair a basket he had trampled when her grandfather visited to check the house's geomancy, sparing him a beating. He tells people to have her guide them to a mountain eatery whose owner is his friend, and to put it on his tab. Lan Yan's 2026 birthday letter says Xiangling's mushroom feast in Chenyu Vale was kept mostly mild because Gaming and Chongyun cannot handle spice.

10.content: The Feiyun Commerce Guild is a longtime agency client, mostly through Xingqiu's elder brother. Xingqiu lent Gaming old texts about the solitary suanni. Xingqiu imagines Gaming as a chivalric hero in black on a moonless road and wants to hear his guard stories. In 5.3 Gaming carried a secret shipment for the Guild from the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor to Chenyu Vale.

11.content: To Gaming, Zhongli is a teahouse regular who listens to storytellers, looks like the smartest man in the room and could talk tea with his father all night. Zhongli praised Gaming to Yip Tak in 4.4 as skilled, kind and selfless, with the spirit of the suanni. Gaming does not know he is the former Geo Archon.

key: The Funeral Parlor Has No Master
12.content: Limited-time Lantern Rite event, January 2025. Gaming greeted the Traveler at the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor while collecting a confidential shipment for the Feiyun Commerce Guild to Chenyu Vale. He worried for a moment that word had leaked, until Paimon explained Xingqiu had told them. The job fitted perfectly with his father's wish that he come home for the holidays. He said the Guild was preparing for the worst while still hoping for the best for Xingqiu's ailing great-grandfather.

key: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon
13.comment: Gaming: Moonchase with the Wind Reader (7.1)
13.content: Limited-time Moonchase Festival event, September to October 2026. Possessed monsters ambushed Gaming's fragile, valuable convoy in Dihua Marsh; Hu Tao, Xingqiu and Chongyun held them off, and the Traveler and Lan Yan, travelling with the recalled soul of her clan founder Lan Junming, the Wind Reader, helped clear the road using Lan Yan's banner and rattan figures. Gaming served everyone tea, promised them a feast at Xinyue Kiosk, ate two plates alone at the Wangshu Inn moon-viewing dinner, and asked the Wind Reader how the Eight Adepts first met: at a roadside tea stop, which delighted him. Hu Tao named him one of the "Three Heroes of Wangshu". He asked the fisherman Jiangxue to teach him Yunlai Swordsmanship; Jiangxue declined and told him to perfect his Wushou footwork. He was away on another escort job for the final part.

14.content: In his Anecdote, the Traveler finds Gaming cooking near Wuwang Hill with a fowl given him by a client and mountain spring water. He makes Golden-Tempered Jade, a dish Leong (from his mother's hometown) said she loved: the fowl is dipped in boiling water, lifted out while he mentally recites a rhyme of festive dishes, repeated three times, then chilled in Mist Flower water and poached at the lowest heat. He admits he skips steps for himself but always follows them to the letter for friends.

15.content: Gaming finds work for the handyman Duqin, helps the busy agency worker Zhigui, fetches medicinal wine for fellow guards, and once had Dip Yeuk give a suanni toy to a boy he had never met because the child liked Wushou Dance. Leong, his father's assistant and a native of his mother's hometown, wrote him festival letters on his father's behalf. Locals always have a dim sum seat for him, as long as he does not try to pay.

16.comment: Gaming: Baizhu, Qiqi and Gaming's injuries
16.content: Baizhu's medicine is Gaming's essential travel kit, and Baizhu has given up on making him careful and taught him to dress his own wounds. Qiqi makes him stretch, convinced his accidents come from stiff joints. His worst injury was a fall from a high pole on his first attempt, and he once feared his career was over.

17.comment: Gaming: Xiangling, Xinyan and Yun Jin
17.content: Gaming loves Xiangling's Black-Back Perch Stew, scraping off the "molten lava sauce" and gasping through it anyway; she brews tea ahead of his visits. He dreams of a rock 'n' roll Wushou show with Xinyan, and considers Yun Jin's Yun-Han Opera Troupe the success he wants for his own troupe.

18.content: Qiaoying Village in Chenyu Vale is famous for tea, including Sunglo and Single-Origin Yauwan. As a small child Gaming missed seeing a famous Yilong Wharf troupe because his father lingered over dim sum; his father hoisted him onto his shoulders, and the stage suanni leapt onto a pillar and locked eyes with him. Afterwards he trained obsessively: eight bamboo baskets fell to his kicks, spoons vanished for drumsticks, and once he danced with a basket of new tea, scattering it, and was chased through the village by his father and met at the door by his mother with a rattan rod. His parents watched him practise through every season, days he now sees only in dreams.
